summary: The Polish market for extracurricular STEM education is robust, driven by high parental emphasis on technical skills and future career prospects. While global competition is intense, localized content, language accessibility (Polish-first instruction), and regional cultural alignment offer a strong moat against international giants. Success depends on moving beyond generic coding to high-engagement, mentor-led models that build community.

strengths: High cultural value placed on technical education in Poland
Lower cost of acquisition compared to Western markets
Ability to build a highly localized curriculum in Polish
Strong pipeline of local IT talent for hiring high-quality instructors
weaknesses: Highly fragmented market with low barrier to entry
Dependency on finding and retaining high-quality, tech-savvy instructors
Potential for churn if the curriculum is not constantly updated
opportunities: Integration of AI and robotics into the standard curriculum
Partnerships with local Polish schools for after-school programs
Expanding to CEE countries with localized versions
threats: Intense price competition from mass-market global platforms
Risk of commoditization of basic coding education
Economic downturn reducing disposable income for extracurriculars

lean_canvas.problem: Lack of high-quality, engaging, and age-appropriate coding education that goes beyond basic tutorials.
lean_canvas.customer_segments: Parents of children aged 7-16 in Poland who value STEM education and are willing to pay for supplemental private tutoring.
lean_canvas.unique_value_proposition: Project-based, mentor-led coding courses that lead to tangible portfolio pieces, delivered entirely in native Polish.
lean_canvas.solution: Live, small-group virtual classrooms with an interactive curriculum and personalized project feedback.
lean_canvas.channels: Social media marketing (Facebook/Instagram parent groups), partnerships with local schools, and content marketing (free webinars).
lean_canvas.revenue_streams: Monthly subscription fees for recurring courses and one-time fees for intensive workshops or summer bootcamps.
lean_canvas.cost_structure: Instructor salaries, software licensing/hosting, customer acquisition costs (ads), and platform maintenance.
lean_canvas.key_metrics: Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR), Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC), Student Churn Rate, and Net Promoter Score (NPS).
lean_canvas.unfair_advantage: Superior localized curriculum that aligns with the Polish education system and a deep network of local expert mentors.

risks.risk: High churn rate due to gamification fatigue
risks.mitigation: Focus on long-term project outcomes and portfolio building rather than simple gamified blocks.
Develop an internal 'train-the-trainer' program and partner with Polish technical universities for internships.

risks.risk: Price wars with established global players
risks.mitigation: Focus on high-touch, live instruction which is harder to commoditize than pre-recorded subscriptions.

next_steps: Validate demand through a low-cost MVP (one-week summer online coding workshop).
Design a 3-tier curriculum (Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced) focusing on Python/Game Dev/Web Dev.
Recruit a core team of 3-5 high-performing CS students as instructors.
Launch a localized digital marketing pilot in a major Polish city to measure CAC.
